_doc: session-guard config. Copy to session-guard.json (git-ignored) and adjust. `~` expands to the guarded user's home (notify.user, or SUDO_USER when run via sudo) — never to the daemon's own $HOME. Directory prefixes must end with '/'. Run `./run.sh --learn 300` to see which processes touch these paths on your machine, then extend `allow`.

_allow_rule_fields.exe_prefix: executable path prefix (string or list); weakest pin, a binary can be placed anywhere
_allow_rule_fields.signing_id_prefix: prefix match on the signing identifier
_allow_rule_fields.team_id: Apple Developer Team ID; strongest pin for third-party software
_allow_rule_fields.cwd: process working directory (string or list, prefix match); live lookup via lsof, use it to pin an interpreter (bun/node/python) to ONE project instead of allowing every script it runs
_allow_rule_fields.cmd_regex: regex on the live `ps` command line; short-lived processes may be gone before lookup, which then does NOT match (fail closed)
_allow_rule_fields._semantics: a rule matches when ALL of its fields match; the first matching rule wins

_exclude_doc: opencode/snapshot/ holds git snapshots of your working trees, read by short-lived `git` children of opencode that exit before a cmd_regex lookup can identify them; codex/skills/ is installed skill content, not session data.

allow.name: opencode
allow._note: opencode ships ad-hoc signed (Identifier=a.out, no team) so only its path can be pinned

_aggregate_doc: every matched event (allowed or not) is also counted per hour x actor x location and appended to <log_dir>/access-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl at this interval; skills/session-guard-report/report.py turns those files into an HTML report. Set notify.macos_notification=false for a quiet, report-only setup.

notify._user_doc: null = SUDO_USER (run.sh) / baked in by install.sh (LaunchDaemon). Set explicitly if that guess is wrong.
notify._command_doc: optional shell command; receives the alert JSON on stdin (webhook, chat bot, ...)
